title: Eagles - Hotel California (guitar solo section) - still cannot calibrate the seventh gate, but exposed a real stem-mixing defect
source: Real bs_roformer_sw stems (bass/drums/guitar) of the solo section, 62.6s. Chart is the Ultimate Guitar official chart, which is written in a DIFFERENT KEY from this audio.
key_note: The CHART is in Bm. This AUDIO is in Dm - a minor third (+3 semitones) above it. Verified: 5 of 5 detected roots are explained by the chart transposed +3, and 0 of 5 at +2 or +4. The pipeline independently called the key D minor at 0.913 confidence, which is correct for this audio.
chords_note: The chart's Bm F# A E / G D Em F#7 transposed +3 to match the audio.
notes: AUDIO KEY DIFFERS FROM THE CHART. Chart is Bm, audio is Dm (+3 semitones). Verified: 5 of 5 detected roots explained at +3, 0 of 5 at +2 or +4. The pipeline independently reported D minor at 0.913 confidence, which is correct for this audio. When a chart and a recording disagree on key, transpose the CHART - the app reports sounding pitch.

THE REAL FINDING: detect_chords sums every pitched non-bass stem into one identity mix, and a loud monophonic LEAD in that sum destroys a chord read that the rhythm stem alone gets right. Measured on this excerpt, with the chart transposed:
identity = guitar only        : 5 roots, A (the V) MISSING, 100% power chords
identity = other only         : 6 roots, ALL correct, zero spurious, 4% power chords
identity = guitar+other+piano : identical to guitar-only - the lead swamps everything
identity = the same three, RMS-equalised before summing: 5 roots, A still missing, 54-72% power chords

So loudness is only part of it: even at equal RMS a sustained lead note is confidently wrong while rhythm chroma is spread across a triad. This is the same SHAPE as the CD-7 bass problem (a loud stem burying the informative one), but the CD-7 remedy - exclude that stem - does not transfer, because on most songs the guitar stem IS the rhythm guitar. Airbourne and Empty Rooms both read fine from guitar-ish content.

DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED. One 62-second solo excerpt is not enough evidence to change how stems are combined for every song, and shipping a change on a single unrepresentative sample is the exact mistake CD-8 made. Recorded here instead.

A possible future signal, cheap to compute and already measured: how many chroma bins a stem holds above half its frame peak. Triads read about 3, a harmonised two-note lead about 2, a single line about 1. On this excerpt guitar=1.76, other=2.13, piano=3.92 (but piano RMS is 0.0015, 34dB below guitar - near silence, so its high count is separation noise). Any such weighting must gate on stem energy first.

WHY IT STILL CANNOT CALIBRATE CHORD_SEVENTH_ABSENCE_RATIO: even from the 'other' stem alone, the V chord appears as exactly ONE 2.4-second run and reads as A5, not A or A7. One run is not a calibration, and a power-chord reading cannot distinguish A from A7 at all. Needs a VERSE or CHORUS section (identical progression, rhythm guitar carrying it, no lead over the top).

Beat grid ruled out: grids forced at 74, 99, 148 bpm and half-time all gave identical roots, the same missing V, and the same 100% power chords. Detected tempo is 99.4bpm at every start_bpm prior, against the chart's 74 - consistent with a different arrangement.
